newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. spurt sparks Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spurt sparks Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened higher on Tuesday after Wall Street's surge on growing confidence about the U.S. Federal Reserve's intentins on interest rates.

The All Ordinaries index was up 15.4 at 2,266.2 in early trading. The September share price index futures contract was up 20 points at 2,273, a 6.8 point premium to the underlying index. Brokers said Wall Street had again provided the impetus for local traders to take the bourse higher although turnover remained at lighter levels.
"Another strong day in the U.S. has given us the push with the leaders all up a few," said a Sydney broker.
RTZ-CRA was an early improver ahead of half year results due on Thursday. On the negative side of the ledger were gold stocks after gold prices eased overnight.
"CRA is seeing some interest ahead of its results with some buying there but not surprisingly the golds have seen their wings trimmed," the broker said.
Against a stronger overall market, the gold index lost 1.2 percent in early trade.
Another standout was transport, telecoms and healthcare group Mayne Nickless. Brokers said investors were continuing to buy up ahead of the Optus Communications float later this year.
Mayne holds a 24.9 percent stake in Optus, Australia's second largest telecomunications company.
Early results came from GIO Insurance which posted a flat full year net profit of A$142.2 million (US$113.6 million). Its shares were firmer with the broader market.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
